29 countries, no routine checks at their shared borders, and it started with five governments in a small village in Luxembourg. Here is when each country joined Schengen.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ On 14 June 1985 five of the ten EEC members, Belgium, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, France and West Germany, signed the agreement at Schengen. The checks didn't actually go until the area was created on 26 March 1995.

2/ Spain and Portugal were there in 1995 too. Italy and Austria followed in 1997 and Greece in 2000. The Nordic countries came in together in 2001, including non-EU Norway and Iceland, both members of the Nordic Passport Union.
3/ The biggest jump came in 2007, when the countries that joined the EU in 2004 entered almost as one, from Estonia down to Slovenia. Non-EU Switzerland joined in 2008 and Liechtenstein in 2011.
4/ Then the waiting room. Croatia got in in 2023. Bulgaria and Romania lifted air and sea border checks on 31 March 2024 and land checks on 1 January 2025, more than 17 years after joining the EU.

5/ Two EU members are still outside. Ireland keeps an opt-out to protect its Common Travel Area with the UK. Cyprus is committed to joining and has aimed for 2026, complicated by the island's division since 1974.
Has Schengen changed the way you travel? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
